MINOR: Delta ships two new untested branches in `_docs_body` (hardcoded config-ref injection and the ROOT containment guard); the pre-existing test-coverage gap now covers more shipped gate logic.

The containment guard silently `continue`s on out-of-ROOT refs with no log/warning, so declared-scope files (`../.github/workflows/structure.yml`, `../.github/workflows/full-sweep.yml`) drop out of the review prompt with no trace that they were considered and skipped.

`seen` dedup keys on the raw ref string before `.resolve()`, so two spellings of the same path (e.g. a hardcoded `config/env-flags.json` plus an `./`-prefixed entry in `affected_files`) are both read and injected.
NIT: The four config refs are item-agnostic and unconditional, so every architect review for any item now injects these files regardless of relevance; the list is also a second hardcoded config path inventory alongside `config/architect-review.json`.
The guard uses `ROOT.resolve() not in p.parents`, which also rejects `ref == ROOT` itself — harmless today but worth a comment since it is a containment assertion others will copy.
SUMMARY: The delta is a small tooling-only change (language rule satisfied) whose traversal guard correctly closes the previously reported out-of-repo read path; the prior MAJOR on out-of-ROOT injection is resolved by this hunk.
No AC in BI-PF-1531 is broken or de-evidenced by this delta (declared file `config/env-flags.json` is untouched; flag default remains `on`).
Top residual risks are silent skipping of declared-scope files and growth of the untested `_docs_body` branch; both are MINOR hardening, not contract-breaking.
